messages.subject: Graph-level attributes
parts:
Chris,
I am able to get the graph level attributes using graph_attr_dt function. But these are the mean global measures. Can you help me with the code to obtain graph attributes for each subject? 
I am trying to get the mean and standard deviation. 

Thank you,
Jaiashre.

messages.author: 638777fa743438d8
messages.subject: Re: Graph-level attributes
parts:
Hi Jaiashre, 

The individual `brainGraph` object (which carries many of the `igraph` graph metrics) should be in the `g[[i]]` list which you've generated (assuming you have followed Chris' steps in the User Manual). It should have thresholds and subject groups nested with that `g[[i]]` list.

It would be great if you can attach some parts of your code or even saving your `g[[i]]` brainGraph object so others can further help you out.

Best, 

Sean

Hi Sean, 

I have provided my code below and also attached my input files. I have been following the user guide v2.0.2. 

#Initialize variables
exclude.subs <- NULL
use.mean <- FALSE
init.vars <- brainGraph_init(atlas='dk', densities=c(0.26), datadir=datadir, modality='thickness', exclude.subs = exclude.subs)
lapply(seq_along(init.vars), function(x) assign(names(init.vars)[x], eval(init.vars[[x]]), envir = .GlobalEnv))

#Global environment
all.dat.resids <- get.resid(lhrh, covars=covars, use.mean=use.mean, exclude='Group')
all.dat.tidy <- all.dat.resids$all.dat.tidy
resids.all <- all.dat.resids$resids.all

#Linear model for each region - excluding the 'Group' column
all.dat.resids <- get.resid(lhrh, covars=covars, use.mean=use.mean, exclude='Group')
all.dat.tidy <- all.dat.resids$all.dat.tidy
resids.all <- all.dat.resids$resids.all

#Correlation matrix
corrs <- lapply(groups, function(x) corr.matrix(resids.all[resids.all$Group == x], densities=densities)) 

#Graph creation - weighted
g <- lapply(corrs, function(x) apply(x$r.thresh, 3, function(y) graph_from_adjacency_matrix(x$R * y, mode= 'undirected' , diag=F, weighted=T)))

# Set relevant graph-, vertex- and edge-level attributes
g <- Map(function(x, y) llply(x, set_brainGraph_attr, atlas=atlas, modality=modality, group=y, .progress='text'), g, as.list(groups))

I don't think my g.list nests the subject level. Can you check? 
Can you also share how you constructed your g.list?

We are looking for subject-level data for power analysis calculations. 

Thank you! I really appreciate your help,

Jaiashre.

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Re: Graph-level attributes
parts:
Hi Jaiashre, unfortunately since you're doing a structural covariance network analysis, you cannot get modularity for each subject. The graphs that are stored in list element "g[[1]]" are all of those for Group 1, where "g[[1]][[1]]" is *Group 1, threshold/density 1*; "g[[1]][[2]]" is *Group 1, threshold/density 2*; and so on.

So, there is no subject-level data to access. Each gray matter region would have to be the same size for that to be possible, but as you know Freesurfer regions are not all equal sizes.

You mention you want the mean and standard deviation for power analysis. For the mean, you can use the observed value; i.e., "g[[1]][[1]]$mod" for example. For the standard deviation, you must do bootstrapping. See Chapter 13.1 of the User Guide for more information on this.

Chris

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Re: Graph-level attributes
parts:
If you are using an atlas in which all regions are not the same size, and you are interested in the inter-regional covariance (of LGI), then yes the same is true.
If *all* ROI's were the same exact size, you could obtain inter-regional covariance (correlation) between all ROI pairs for each subject.
For functional data, you *can* do what you want, if you calculate inter-regional correlation in the mean time series per subject.
